note: Every non-ASCII character the books' MAIN FONT sets, read from the UNICODE cmap subtables of the four Latin Modern Roman text faces (regular, bold, italic, bold-italic -- identical, 794 codepoints each) and verified by rendering. A character NOT in this list and NOT given a \newunicodechar mapping in the book's preamble reaches the reader as a missing glyph, which is a CI failure and has happened twice: ae-with-macron in Latin (HL-C214) and open-o in Bengali (HL-C223). THIS LIST WAS CURATED UNTIL VERSION 2 AND THEREFORE HAD HOLES. It held 123 of the 530 characters the font actually sets -- 121 until the ordinal tranche noticed two of them -- so a character the font supports read as unsupported and was unwritable in every book: 1.º was unwritable across the corpus until the ordinal tranche added U+00AA and U+00BA by hand, and german/CHANGELOG.md records capital Ü being avoided for the same reason while the font has had it all along. A curated allow-list fails in exactly one direction -- silently, against the author -- so this is now the font's answer rather than a selection from it.
font: Latin Modern Roman (LMRoman10-Regular and family, version 2.004)

excluded: ASCII (U+0000..U+007F), 95 of the 794 -- this list has always been the non-ASCII half, and ASCII is never at risk.
Private Use Area (U+E000..U+F8FF), 167 -- Latin Modern's internal glyph slots for oldstyle figures and text-companion forms. They are font-internal, not characters anybody may write.

U+00A0 NO-BREAK SPACE and U+00AD SOFT HYPHEN, 2 -- the only characters in Unicode categories C* or Z* the Unicode cmap carries outside the Private Use Area. Both are invisible in the page and U+00A0's glyph has no outline at all, so blessing them here would let an invisible character into the corpus under a claim about rendering.
generatedFrom.cmapNote: The Unicode subtables only -- (3,1) and (0,3), both format 4 and both 794 codepoints. Each face ALSO carries a (1,0) Mac Roman format 6 subtable of 213 entries, whose keys are Mac Roman BYTE VALUES and not codepoints. Unioning it in is a real trap and this file walked into it once: it makes 0x80..0x9F look like mapped characters when they are the C1 control range, and inflates the count from 794 to 828. The package's own font reader in loader.ts parses formats 4 and 12 and ignores format 6, so Unicode-only is also what every other font in this corpus is measured by.
generatedFrom.kept: 794 - 95 - 167 - 2 = 530, which is the length of `characters` below.

verification: Every one of the 407 characters version 2 adds was RENDERED, not merely read out of the cmap. Two passes with XeLaTeX and \setmainfont{Latin Modern Roman}: a listing document reported 0 'Missing character' lines, and a one-character-per-page document was rasterised and each page measured for ink, so a cmap entry pointing at a blank glyph could not pass as support. Four characters measured zero ink at 72dpi and were re-rendered at 600dpi -- U+00AF, U+0331, U+0332 and U+2423, all thin single strokes -- and all four set. The one glyph in the cmap with no outline, U+00A0, is excluded above.

smallCapsGap.note: The two SMALL CAPS faces (lmromancaps10-regular, lmromancaps10-oblique) carry 787 Unicode codepoints rather than 794, and these six are what they drop -- a small-caps face has no lowercase long s and no lowercase f-ligatures. NO BOOK IN THIS CORPUS USES SMALL CAPS: \textsc and \scshape appear zero times across every book/ directory, and the preamble's SmallCapsFont is declared and never selected. If that changes, these six become face-dependent and this gate stops being a single answer.

howToAdd: DO NOT hand-add. Regenerate: read the cmap of the four text faces above, intersect them, drop ASCII, the Private Use Area and categories Cc/Cf/Zl/Zp/Zs, and render the result before committing it. If a character is absent from the font -- capital eszett U+1E9E, open o U+0254 and ae-with-macron U+01E3 all are -- then either choose one the font has or add a \newunicodechar mapping to EVERY book preamble that uses it, which is how the Indic romanization marks are handled. Adding a character here that the font lacks turns this file from a record into a wrong answer.
